subsystems.name: Cryogenic sample container
subsystems.role: holds the sample below the temperature at which its ices sublimate, for years.

subsystems.name: Sample acquisition tool
subsystems.role: cuts or cores volatile-rich material from a comet nucleus without warming it.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus and propulsion
subsystems.role: flies to the comet, matches its orbit and carries the sample home.
parts: deep-space power (RTG or large solar arrays)

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps the cryostat cold while the rest of the spacecraft is in sunlight.

subsystems.name: Earth return capsule
subsystems.role: survives re-entry and keeps the cold chain intact until landing.

subsystems.name: Curation and cold chain
subsystems.role: transfers the sample from the capsule to a laboratory without thawing it.
parts: analytical instruments cooled to sample temperature

buildSteps.title: Pick a target
buildSteps.detail: Choose an accessible, volatile-rich comet — most likely a Jupiter-family comet on a short-period orbit that a spacecraft can reach and match velocities with.

buildSteps.title: Design and test the cryostat
buildSteps.detail: A vacuum flask with a cryocooler is tested in a thermal-vacuum chamber, proving it can hold its internal temperature for years of cruise.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Structure, propulsion, power, communications and the sampling tool are integrated and the cryostat is mounted with a dedicated power and data feed.

buildSteps.title: Fly to the comet
buildSteps.detail: Launch, then use gravity assists or solar-electric thrusting to rendezvous — a matching, not a flyby, since a flyby is far too fast to sample.

buildSteps.title: Map and choose a site
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, radar and spectrometers find a patch of exposed or shallowly buried ice, avoiding jets and unstable rubble.

buildSteps.title: Acquire and seal the sample
buildSteps.detail: Because the nucleus has almost no gravity, the spacecraft either anchors itself or briefly touches down. The tool cuts or cores a few centimetres to centimetres-deep sample, moves it into the cryostat and seals it — ideally without ever letting it warm or see air.

buildSteps.title: Cruise home cold
buildSteps.detail: The cryocooler runs continuously for the return leg; the sample must stay below the sublimation point of water ice for the whole trip.

buildSteps.title: Re-enter and recover
buildSteps.detail: The capsule separates, survives re-entry, parachutes down and is recovered quickly. Re-entry heating is the hardest moment for a cryogenic payload.

buildSteps.title: Transfer to a cold lab
buildSteps.detail: The sealed container is moved into a cryogenic curation facility, where it is opened and analysed while still cold.

prerequisites.why: flight cryocoolers exist for infrared telescopes, but running one reliably for many years while insulating a sample container is a harder requirement.

prerequisites.tech: Rendezvous with a small, outgassing body
prerequisites.why: Rosetta orbited and landed on comet 67P, and sample return from near-Earth asteroids has been achieved by Hayabusa2 and OSIRIS-REx — but nobody has sampled a comet nucleus.
nobody has yet drilled into or cored a comet nucleus; the material is fragile, outgassing and mechanically unpredictable.
Stardust returned comet dust at ambient temperature; no capsule has ever carried a cryogenic payload through re-entry.
cold curation capability is limited, and most laboratory analysis instruments are not designed to run with a freezing sample inside.

pathway.milestone: concept studies; a comet sample-return concept reached the final of NASA's New Frontiers 4 competition in the 2010s but was not chosen
pathway.unlocks: a realistic mission design, cost estimate and list of the technologies that must be matured.

pathway.milestone: technology demonstration: a compact, flight-rated cryogenic sampler tested on the ground and in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a sample container can survive launch, years of cruise and re-entry without thawing.

pathway.milestone: a comet rendezvous sample return with cold, though possibly not fully cryogenic, preservation
pathway.unlocks: the first known comet nucleus material in a laboratory, plus the operational experience to do it colder.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated cryogenic sample-return mission with a ground-based cold curation and analysis network
pathway.unlocks: direct measurement of primordial solar-system ices and organics, informing models of how Earth got its water.
